title: A Rainy Day in Saigon
titleVi: Một ngày mưa ở Sài Gòn

script.textEn: My name is Mai, and I want to tell you about a rainy day in my city.
In Saigon, it rains almost every afternoon in the rainy season.
One day last month, I was walking home from school.
The sky was dark, and the wind was very strong.
Suddenly, it started to rain very hard.
I did not have an umbrella, so I ran to a small coffee shop.
The shop was full of people, all waiting for the rain to stop.
I bought a cup of hot milk tea and sat near the window.
Outside, motorbikes were driving slowly through the water.
Some streets were full of water, almost like small rivers.
A little boy was playing in the rain with his friends.
They were laughing and running, and they did not care about the rain.
After one hour, the rain stopped, and the sun came out.
The streets were wet, but everything looked fresh and clean.
I walked home and felt very happy.
Rainy days in Saigon are noisy and busy, but I love them.

options: Every afternoon in the rainy season
questions.correctAnswer: Every afternoon in the rainy season
questions.explanationVi: Đáp án nằm ở dòng 2: 'it rains almost every afternoon in the rainy season'.

questions.explanationVi: Dòng 11-12 nói cậu bé 'laughing and running' — rất vui, không buồn.

questions.explanationVi: Dòng 15: 'I walked home and felt very happy.'

script.textEn: My grandmother lives in a small village in the Mekong Delta.
She has a beautiful garden behind her house.
Every morning, she wakes up at five o'clock to work in the garden.
She grows many kinds of vegetables: morning glory, herbs, and beans.
She also has fruit trees: mango, papaya, and banana trees.
I visit her every summer, and I love helping in the garden.
She teaches me how to plant seeds and water the plants.
She says, 'Plants are like children. They need love and care.'
In the afternoon, we pick fresh vegetables for dinner.
My grandmother cooks the best soup with vegetables from her garden.
After dinner, we sit outside and drink tea.
She tells me stories about her life when she was young.
Her garden is not big, but it gives food to our whole family.
She never buys vegetables at the market.
I want to have a garden like hers when I grow up.
Her garden teaches me to be patient and to love nature.

options: In a small village in the Mekong Delta
questions.correctAnswer: In a small village in the Mekong Delta
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 1 nói rõ bà sống ở 'a small village in the Mekong Delta'.

questions.correctAnswer: To be patient and love nature
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 16: 'Her garden teaches me to be patient and to love nature.'

script.textEn: Last weekend, my friend Lan took me to a night market in Da Lat.
The market opens at five in the evening and closes at midnight.
When we arrived, the market was full of lights and people.
The air smelled of grilled corn, baked sweet potatoes, and hot soy milk.
First, we walked around and looked at the clothes shops.
Lan bought a warm jacket because Da Lat is cold at night.
Then we stopped at a food stall to eat grilled rice paper.
It was hot and crispy, and it cost only fifteen thousand dong.
After eating, we drank hot soy milk to warm our hands.
We met an old woman selling flowers by the road.
She gave us two small roses and wished us a happy evening.
We took many photos of the colorful lights.
At ten o'clock, we were tired, so we walked back to our hotel.
The night market was busy, noisy, and full of delicious food.
I will never forget that wonderful evening in Da Lat.
If you visit Da Lat, you must go to the night market.

questions.explanationVi: Dòng 2: 'The market opens at five in the evening and closes at midnight.'

questions.explanationVi: Dòng 6: 'Lan bought a warm jacket because Da Lat is cold at night.'

title: The Man Who Planted a Forest

script.textEn: Today I want to tell you an amazing true story about a man in India.
His name is Jadav Payeng, and people call him the Forest Man of India.
When he was sixteen years old, he saw something that changed his life.
After a big flood, he found many dead snakes on a river island.
The snakes had died because there were no trees to give them shade.
Jadav decided to plant trees on that empty island.
Every day for more than forty years, he planted trees and took care of them.
At first, people laughed at him and said he was crazy.
But he did not stop. He kept planting, one tree at a time.
Slowly, the empty island turned into a thick green forest.
Today, that forest is bigger than 500 football fields.
Tigers, elephants, deer, and hundreds of birds now live there.
Jadav still lives in a small hut in his forest.
He says he will keep planting trees until his last day.
His story teaches us that one person can change the world.
You do not need to be rich or famous to make a difference.
You only need patience, love for nature, and the courage to start.

questions.correctAnswer: One person with patience can change the world
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 15-17 nêu rõ thông điệp: một người cũng có thể thay đổi thế giới.

script.textEn: We spend about one third of our lives sleeping, but why do we need sleep?
Scientists have studied sleep for many years, and here is what they found.
First, sleep helps our brain save important memories.
During the day, our brain collects a lot of information.
At night, while we sleep, the brain organizes this information.
That is why students remember lessons better after a good night's sleep.
Second, sleep helps our body repair itself.
When we sleep, our muscles grow and our immune system becomes stronger.
People who do not sleep enough get sick more easily.
Third, sleep controls our feelings.
If you sleep badly, you may feel angry or sad for no clear reason.
Most adults need seven to nine hours of sleep every night.
But many people sleep much less because of phones and work stress.
Looking at a phone screen before bed makes it harder to fall asleep.
Experts suggest turning off screens one hour before bedtime.
Reading a book or listening to calm music can help you sleep better.
So tonight, put your phone away early and give your brain the rest it needs.

questions.correctAnswer: Because sleep helps the brain organize information
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 3-6 giải thích não sắp xếp thông tin khi ngủ.

questions.explanationVi: Dòng 14: nhìn màn hình điện thoại trước khi ngủ khiến khó ngủ hơn.

options: Turning off screens one hour before bed
questions.correctAnswer: Turning off screens one hour before bed
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 15: 'turning off screens one hour before bedtime'.

title: The Floating Markets of the Mekong

script.textEn: In the Mekong Delta of Vietnam, there is a special kind of market.
It is called a floating market, because all the shops are on boats.
Every morning before sunrise, hundreds of boats gather on the river.
Each boat sells something different: pineapples, watermelons, vegetables, or fish.
To show what they sell, sellers hang a sample from a tall bamboo pole.
For example, if you see pineapples hanging high, that boat sells pineapples.
Buyers come in small boats and move from seller to seller.
Some boats are like floating restaurants, selling hot noodle soup and coffee.
You can eat breakfast right on the river while watching the sunrise.
The most famous floating markets are Cai Rang and Phong Dien in Can Tho.
In the past, these markets were the main way people traded goods.
Today, roads and supermarkets are more common, so the markets are smaller.
But they are still an important part of local culture and tourism.
Many visitors come to see this unique way of life.
If you wake up early and visit, you will see Vietnam at its most lively.
The floating market is not just a market; it is a living tradition.

options: All the shops are on boats
questions.correctAnswer: All the shops are on boats
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 2: 'all the shops are on boats'.

questions.correctAnswer: To see this unique way of life
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 14: 'Many visitors come to see this unique way of life.'

script.textEn: Imagine you receive a letter from yourself, written ten years in the future.
What would it say? This is a popular writing exercise in many schools.
Last year, a teacher in Hanoi asked her students to write such letters.
One student, Nam, wrote something that surprised everyone.
He wrote: 'Dear Nam, I hope you stopped playing games all night.'
'I hope you started learning English seriously, like you promised.'
'Do you remember the English contest you were afraid to join?'
'In my time, you joined it, and you won second prize.'
'That prize gave you the confidence to try many new things.'
When the teacher read the letter, the whole class was quiet.
Nam explained that writing the letter helped him see his goals clearly.
After that day, he really did start studying English every morning.
Six months later, he joined the English contest at his school.
He did not win, but he was proud that he had tried.
The teacher says the exercise works because it connects today with tomorrow.
When you imagine your future self, your present choices become clearer.
So why not try it? Write a letter to yourself, ten years from now.

questions.correctAnswer: Write a letter from their future self
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 2-3: bài tập viết thư từ chính mình trong tương lai.

options: He joined it and won second prize
questions.correctAnswer: He joined it and won second prize
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 8: 'you joined it, and you won second prize.'

questions.explanationVi: Dòng 14: 'He did not win, but he was proud that he had tried.'

options: Because it connects today with tomorrow
questions.correctAnswer: Because it connects today with tomorrow
questions.explanationVi: Dòng 15: 'it connects today with tomorrow'.

title: The Psychology of Habits
titleVi: Tâm lý học về thói quen

script.textEn: Why is it so easy to start a new habit, but so hard to keep it?
Psychologists say the answer lies in how our brains save energy.
The brain loves patterns because patterns require less thinking.
When you repeat an action in the same situation, the brain turns it into a habit.
A habit has three parts: a cue, a routine, and a reward.
The cue is the trigger, like feeling stressed after work.
The routine is what you do, like eating a snack or checking your phone.
The reward is the good feeling you get afterwards.
To build a good habit, experts suggest starting extremely small.
Instead of 'read for one hour', start with 'read one page'.
Small actions are easy, so your brain does not resist them.
Then connect the new habit to something you already do.
For example: 'After I brush my teeth, I will read one page.'
Research shows it takes about two months for a habit to become automatic.
Most people fail because they try to change too much at once.
Remember: you do not need motivation to start; you need a system.
Design your environment, start tiny, and let repetition do the rest.

questions.explanationVi: Dòng 3: 'patterns require less thinking'.

questions.explanationVi: Dòng 5: 'A habit has three parts: a cue, a routine, and a reward.'

questions.explanationVi: Dòng 14: 'it takes about two months for a habit to become automatic.'

title: Hoi An: The Trading Port of Asia
titleVi: Hội An: Thương cảng của châu Á

script.textEn: Four hundred years ago, Hoi An was one of the busiest ports in Asia.
Ships from Japan, China, India, and Europe all stopped here to trade.
Japanese merchants built a beautiful covered bridge, which still stands today.
Chinese traders built assembly halls with colorful dragons and detailed carvings.
The town became a place where many cultures met and mixed together.
Local people learned to cook with new spices from foreign ships.
They also learned new ways of building houses and making clothes.
But in the 1800s, the river became too shallow for large ships.
Trade moved to Da Nang, and Hoi An slowly became quiet.
For almost two hundred years, the town was forgotten by the world.
Ironically, this forgetfulness saved its old buildings from destruction.
While other cities rebuilt with concrete, Hoi An kept its wooden houses.
In 1999, UNESCO recognized Hoi An as a World Heritage Site.
Today, millions of visitors come to walk its lantern-lit streets.
The town that lost its trade found a new life in its own history.
Hoi An teaches us that sometimes, being left behind is a kind of luck.

title: What AI Cannot Do
titleVi: Những điều AI không làm được

script.textEn: Artificial intelligence can now write essays, paint pictures, and even pass exams.
Many people worry that AI will replace human workers in every field.
But there are important things that AI still cannot do, and may never do well.
First, AI does not truly understand meaning; it only predicts patterns in words.
It can write a poem about sadness, but it has never felt sad.
Second, AI cannot take real responsibility for its decisions.
When a doctor makes a difficult choice, she carries the moral weight of it.
A machine feels no guilt and learns no wisdom from its mistakes.
Third, AI struggles with genuine creativity that breaks all the rules.
It mixes existing ideas very well, but revolutionary ideas often come from human rebellion.
Think of artists and scientists who were called crazy before they were called geniuses.
Finally, AI cannot build deep trust between people.
A student remembers a teacher who believed in him, not the software that graded him.
This does not mean we should fear or reject AI.
It means we should use AI for what it does best: handling routine work.
And we should protect what makes us human: empathy, courage, and conscience.
The future belongs not to humans or machines alone, but to humans with machines.
